name: Entropy Distribution Curve
description: Analyzes the statistical unpredictability (entropy) of token sequences across a text. AI models generate text within a narrow, optimized entropy band, whereas human writing features erratic bursts of high and low unpredictability.
mechanism: In Information Theory, 'entropy' measures the unpredictability of a sequence. Human writing is highly irregular: a writer might string together several highly predictable clichés (low entropy) followed immediately by a wildly creative, lexically dense metaphor or an obscure technical term (high entropy). This creates a jagged, volatile entropy distribution curve over the length of the document. Large Language Models, however, generate text by continuously picking the most statistically probable next token, modulated by a fixed 'Temperature' setting. Because they mathematically optimize for fluency and coherence at every step, the entropy (unpredictability) of AI text remains remarkably stable and uniform across the entire document. This method calculates the Shannon entropy using a sliding window across the text, mapping the statistical distribution and its variance. A text with an exceptionally smooth, uniform entropy distribution—lacking the extreme peaks (creative spikes) and deep valleys (cliché repetition) typical of human cognition—is mathematically proven to be algorithmically generated.
useCase: Best used on long-form content (essays, articles, reports) where statistical distribution patterns can clearly separate the 'machined smoothness' of AI from the 'erratic rhythm' of humans.
strengths:
• Highly mathematically objective; does not rely on semantic understanding, making it entirely language-agnostic and robust against varying topics.
• Effectively exposes the underlying mathematical constraints (like Top-P and Temperature) of the specific LLM used for generation.
• Extremely difficult for a human or basic prompting (e.g., 'write unpredictably') to bypass, as humans cannot consciously calculate and manipulate token probabilities.
limitations:
• Fails on very short texts (less than 150 words) because statistical distribution curves require a sufficiently large sample size to reveal uniform variance.
• Human-written texts that are heavily edited, homogenized by corporate committees, or heavily paraphrased may exhibit artificially smoothed entropy.
• Does not analyze the actual meaning of the text, only the statistical surprise-value of its components.
parameters:
Analysis: Sliding Window Shannon Entropy & Coefficient of Variation (CV)
Metric: Standard Deviation of Entropy Distribution vs Baseline Average
Output: 0-100 Entropy Uniformity (Algorithmic Smoothness) Score
accuracy: High — 78-86% on medium-to-long texts. It is one of the most reliable and deeply technical signatures of machine-generated token sequences.

references.title: Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.

source: Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.; Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
